title: attention: interleaved-dequant prefetch optimizer and kernel scheduler handoff
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Improves throughput for quantized attention by optimizing dequant/prefetch ordering and kernel handoff heuristics; safe rollout with canary by default.
description:
Motivation: In long-sequence and chat workloads we observed stalls caused by the existing two-stage dequant -> kernel dispatch pattern. Large KV-cache lookups frequently forced backend transfers that serialized with kernel uploads, increasing p95 latency on INT8/FP8 mixed paths. This PR introduces an "interleaved dequant + prefetch" optimization and a small scheduler handoff that reduces end-to-end stalls and improves KV cache locality.

Design summary: single-pass inspector (runtime/scheduler/interleave_inspector) walks per-request KV usage hints and issues prefetch requests concurrently while the per-layer dequant step is scheduled. The kernel_router was augmented to accept a "prefetch affinity" hint so that when the dequant completes the kernel can be enqueued to the same GPU/stream to avoid device-to-device shuffles. We also added a light-weight soft-fence that allows the continuous-batcher to overlap next-token inputs with backend prefetch operations for re-used KV slices.

Key changes: modified kernel_router.cc to accept affinity tokens and a small RMQ to track in-flight prefetches; added interleave_prefetch_pass.cc which coordinates dequant + kv prefetch ordering and emits runtime hints; updated kv_cache.cc to expose an async peek API used by the inspector; tuned continuous_batcher to allow speculative enqueues when prefetch affinity is present. Minor API additions are internal-only and protected by a runtime feature flag: redwood.runtime.experimental.interleave_dequant_prefetch.

Benchmarks: microbench (bert-large, seq_len=2048) on n1-standard + A100 profile shows throughput +18% and p95 latency -12% for INT8-smoothquant path vs main. End-to-end chat scenario (gpt-3 style, multi-turn 4k tokens accumulated) shows 22% token/sec improvement and 9% lower tail latency when canaryed on dedicated pools. Memory overhead is negligible (<1% resident increase) due to reusing prefetch buffers and avoiding duplicate copies.

Compatibility and safety: the change is opt-in by runtime flag and guarded by kernel compatibility checks (INT8/FP8 smoothquant variants only). If affinity hints cannot be honored (heterogeneous pool or capacity constraints) the scheduler falls back to pre-existing routing. We added health counters and rollout metrics to Console: interleave.prefetch.hits, interleave.prefetch.fallbacks, interleave.kernel.handoff_latency.

Testing: unit tests for new inspector logic and async kv peek were added; integration perf harness added bench_attn_interleave.py for CI perf regression. Stress tests run in perf-lab with mixed precision loads.

Deployment plan: staged rollout: feature flag enabled on canary pool -> observe metrics for 72h -> gradual ramp to 25% -> 100% if no regressions. Rollback is a single flag flip.

Related: addresses ENG-2419 (reduce dequant-induced stalls) and partially complements ENG-2567 (kv-query locality improvements).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) how does the inspector scale with large request fanout? (2) can we avoid the extra allocation in async kv peek?

Maya Patel: For (1) inspector is O(#kv_slices) and we cap hints to a configurable window (default 8 slices). For (2) we reused pinned scratch buffers from the allocator pool; allocation path is hot but pooled so amortized cost is low. Added note in code and a new perf test showing negligible allocation overhead.
Rosa Alvarez: Need stronger guards for mixed-precision fallbacks — please add a metrics signal when the scheduler falls back to old path.
Maya Patel: Added interleave.prefetch.fallbacks and increment points in kernel_router and inspector. Also added an e2e test that forces fallback and asserts metrics are emitted.
Devon McCarthy: CI flagged a race in prefetch completion; see my comment on interleave_inspector.cc:line78. Please add ordering fence.
Maya Patel: Added soft-fence using the runtime stream semaphore; updated tests to cover the race. CI green on rerun.
